- Materials expertise: broad capabilities across paper, metal, plastic, recycled, and bio-based materials, including recyclable plastics.
- Business strategy: three pillars—focused portfolio, differentiated capabilities, and aspiration to be the leading global packaging company; focused portfolio targets primary packaging for fast-moving consumer goods, benefits from favorable industry structure and attractive growth, and creates multiple competitive advantages through leadership, scale, and innovation.

structure.title: Business
structure.heading: Item 1. Business
structure.start_phrase: Amcor plc (ARBN 630 385 278) is a public limited company incorporated under the Laws of the Bailiwick of Jersey.
structure.summary:
- Company overview: Amcor plc, a Jersey-incorporated, global leader in responsible packaging for food, beverage, pharmaceutical/medical, home and personal care, and other products; long history with roots in Australia and the U.S.; innovation- and sustainability-led.
- Sustainability focus: Industry-first 2018 pledge for all packaging to be designed for recycling/composting/reuse by 2025 and to increase recycled content; strategy anchored in product innovation, consumer participation, and infrastructure; partnerships across the value chain; annual ~$100M R&D spend; advancing circular economy; EnviroAction program improving energy, water, and waste; science-based targets with net zero by 2050 and targets submitted to SBTi in 2023.
- Differentiated solutions and materials expertise: Broad portfolio spanning paper, metal, plastic, recycled, and bio-based materials; emphasis on designing high-performance, more sustainable packaging; continual investment in design, science, and manufacturing.
- Business strategy: Three pillars—focused portfolio, differentiated capabilities (“The Amcor Way”: Talent, Commercial Excellence, Operational Leadership, Innovation, Cash & Capital Discipline), and the aspiration to be the leading global packaging company; value creation via strong cash flow, dividends, organic growth, targeted M&A, and buybacks; focus on primary packaging for FMCG with attractive industry structure and growth.
- Segments: Two reportable segments under ASC 280.
  - Flexibles: Global supplier of plastic, aluminum, and fiber-based flexible packaging; ~35,000 employees, 166 facilities in 37 countries; ~76% of FY2023 net sales.
  - Rigid Packaging: Americas-focused rigid containers and related products; ~5,000 employees, 52 facilities in 11 countries; ~24% of FY2023 net sales.
- Marketing, distribution, and competition: Primarily direct sales supported by technical teams; global footprint; no customer >10% of sales in last three years; competitive factors include service, sustainability, innovation, quality, and price; numerous global competitors named.
- Backlog and working capital: Manage inventory to balance cost and service; manufacturing backlog not significant.
- Raw materials: Key inputs include polymer resins/films, paper, inks, solvents, adhesives, aluminum, chemicals; diversified suppliers; manage shortages through supplier/customer collaboration; generally pass through input cost changes via contracts and other mechanisms.
- Intellectual property: Extensive global portfolio of patents, trademarks, and trade secrets; no single IP right is individually material.
- Sustainability and innovation detail: >1,000 active patents; global Innovation Centers; >1,000 R&D professionals; collaborations with customers, suppliers, NGOs, startups, and cross-industry groups to improve recycling/reuse and advocate standards and infrastructure.
- Regulatory environment: Subject to health, safety, environmental, and other regulations across jurisdictions; believes it is in substantial compliance but acknowledges evolving regulations and potential liabilities; references contingencies and risk factors.
- Seasonality and cash flow: Operations not materially seasonal; cash flow from operations typically lower in first half and higher in second half due to working capital and payment timing.
- Research and development: Cross-referenced to sustainability and accounting notes; ongoing investment beyond core R&D spend.
- Human capital management: ~41,000 employees globally (30% North America, 30% Europe, 20% Latin America, 20% Asia Pacific); ~45% under collective bargaining; safety as a core value with 31% injury reduction and 69% of sites injury-free in FY2023; robust talent, performance, and leadership development programs (LTO, SLDP, EDP 2.0, Masterclass); DEI strategy focused on inclusive leadership, unbiased talent processes, and sharing best practices; employee engagement surveys; strong ethics and Code of Business Conduct with global training.
- Executive leadership: Lists key executives, roles, and tenure, including CEO Ronald Delia and leaders across finance, HR, legal, and business units.
- Investor information: SEC filings accessible via SEC website and Amcor’s investor relations site; availability of 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, and related filings; website information not incorporated by reference.

structure.title: Risk Factors
structure.heading: Item 1A. Risk Factors
structure.start_phrase:
The following factors, as well as factors described elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, or in other filings by us with the Securities
and Exchange Commission, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, results of operations, or cash flows.
structure.summary:
- Document scope: Item 1A. Risk Factors outlining risks that could materially affect the company’s business, financial condition, results of operations, and cash flows, including known and emerging uncertainties.

- Strategic risks:
  - Shifts in consumer demand and packaging preferences (cost, regulation, health, environmental and social concerns) potentially reducing demand or rendering products obsolete; challenges forecasting demand and delivering timely, cost-effective innovation.
  - Dependence on key customers and effects of customer consolidation, including potential loss of volume, pricing pressure, relocation due to physical climate risks, and changing regulatory environments.
  - Intense competition on price, innovation, sustainability, service, and quality; risk of disruptive technologies by competitors.
  - Growth execution risk: limits to organic expansion, product innovation hurdles, identifying and completing attractive acquisitions, integrating acquired businesses, and potential impairments from minority investments.

- Operational risks:
  - Global economic conditions, including the Russia-Ukraine conflict and inflation, affecting demand, pricing, supply chains, and financing; divestiture of Russian operations and reinvestment plans; risk of further regional unrest.
  - International operations complexity and instability (legal, regulatory, tax, FX controls, sanctions, contract enforceability, political/social unrest, health crises), especially in emerging markets; sanctions compliance risk.
  - Raw material, energy, and input price volatility and supply shortages (polymers, paper, inks, solvents, aluminum, chemicals; energy in Europe); trade policy/tariff impacts (e.g., aluminum duties); limits of pricing pass-throughs and timing lags.
  - Commercial risks: production disruptions, supplier concentration and shortages, freight and logistics constraints, climate-related impacts on customers’ supply chains (e.g., meat packaging volumes), and heightened counterparty credit risk in volatile economies.
  - Health crises (e.g., COVID-19) disrupting operations, supply chains, labor, costs, and demand.
  - Talent risk: attracting, developing, and retaining executives and skilled workforce amid labor shortages, wage inflation, and demographic shifts.
  - Operational EHS obligations: compliance costs, potential liabilities, remediation, fines, and climate-related regulatory changes increasing costs.
  - Labor disputes: significant union representation, risk of strikes/work stoppages and challenges renewing collective bargaining agreements.
  - Climate change: physical risks to facilities and supply chains, insurance availability/costs, and altered customer demand patterns.

- Information technology and cybersecurity risks:
  - Cyber threats (including nation-state actors) and data breaches impacting operations, confidentiality, compliance with evolving privacy laws (U.S., EU, China), and reputation; third-party and supply chain cyber risks.
  - IT systems failures or disruptions (including cloud/third-party systems) from outages, upgrades, attacks, or disasters; limits of disaster recovery.

- Financial risks:
  - Interest rate exposure: variable-rate debt increasing borrowing costs; hedge effectiveness and counterparty risk; impacts on working capital programs.
  - Indebtedness and credit ratings: $6.7B debt, reliance on capital markets and facilities, potential downgrades raising costs and limiting access; structural subordination at non-guarantor subsidiaries.
  - Foreign exchange risk: transactional and translational exposures, especially EUR/GBP/CHF/AUD/CNY/BRL vs USD; Argentina highly inflationary accounting; pass-through lags on USD-denominated inputs; hedge effectiveness and counterparty risk.
  - Goodwill and intangible asset impairment risk from changes in rates, growth, or strategy.
  - Internal controls: SOX 404 compliance risks, potential misstatements, restatements, regulatory scrutiny, and stock price impact.
  - Insurance coverage limitations and captive insurer exposure to large claims.

- Legal and compliance risks:
  - Intellectual property: ability to protect IP globally (especially in emerging markets), costs of enforcement/defense, and potential infringement claims.
  - Litigation and regulatory proceedings, including product liability and matters related to actions taken due to geopolitical events.
  - ESG scrutiny: stakeholder expectations, ability to meet sustainability targets (e.g., SBTi and net-zero by 2050), customer supply-chain emissions requirements, reputational and market impacts; rising disclosure and compliance costs (e.g., EU CSRD, proposed SEC climate rules).
  - Environmental, health, and safety regulation: potential bans/restrictions, EPR schemes, taxes/fees on packaging, mandated PCR content, emissions regulation increasing operating costs; compliance requirements in highly regulated healthcare and food packaging.
  - Tax risks: audits, law changes (including OECD BEPS), and earnings mix shifts affecting effective tax rate.

- Jurisdictional and governance risks:
  - Incorporation in Jersey, Channel Islands: differences from U.S. corporate law, potential changes in Jersey law, and implications for shareholder rights.
  - Enforcement challenges for U.S. shareholders due to non-U.S. assets/officers, jurisdictional limits, and exclusive forum provisions centered on the Royal Court of Jersey for certain internal affairs claims.

structure.heading: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.start_phrase: Management’s Discussion and Analysis should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and related Notes included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
structure.summary:
- Scope and context: Management’s Discussion and Analysis for FY2023 vs. FY2022, to be read with the Consolidated Financial Statements; prior-year MD&A (FY2022 vs. FY2021) incorporated by reference.
- Company overview: Amcor is a global packaging leader serving food, beverage, pharma/medical, home/personal care; focus on lightweight, recyclable, reusable, and recycled-content packaging; FY2023 sales of $14.7B across 218 locations in 40+ countries.
- Economic/market conditions: Ongoing raw material and resin volatility, elevated inflation in energy, fuel, and labor; rapid interest rate rises increasing variable-rate interest expense; Russia-Ukraine conflict impacts; customer destocking and softer consumer demand in FY2023 with gradual improvement expected in FY2024, albeit uncertain.
- Russia-Ukraine and restructuring:
  - Suspended Ukraine operations; sold Russian business on Dec 23, 2022 for $365M net cash plus ~$65M repatriated; pre-tax net gain $215M; previous $90M impairment in Q4 FY2022.
  - 2023 Restructuring Plan to invest $110–$130M of proceeds in cost savings; total Plan net expenses expected $200–$220M; FY2023 charges: $65M employee, $13M fixed assets, $10M other, $6M related; ~$25M cash outflow to date; targeted ~$50M annualized pre-tax savings from Russia-related actions by end of FY2025.
- Other notable events:
  - COVID-19: No significant ongoing restrictions; China lockdown unwind dampened FY2023 demand.
  - South Africa fire (Durban): FY2022–2023 total expenses $55M pre-insurance; $46M insurance proceeds.
  - 2019 Bemis Integration Plan: Completed FY2022; exceeded $180M synergy target by ~10%; total cost $253M; net cash outflows $170M.
  - Highly inflationary accounting (Argentina): FX transaction losses of $24M (FY2023) vs. $16M (FY2022).
- Consolidated results:
  - Net sales $14,694M (+1%); underlying change flat after $776M raw material pass-through, $(426)M FX, $(207)M disposals; price/mix +3%, volumes −3%.
  - Gross profit $2,725M (−3%); margin 18.5% vs. 19.4% (impacted by raw material pass-through and disposals).
  - Operating income $1,508M (10.3% margin) vs. $1,239M.
  - Net income attributable to Amcor $1,048M (+30%); drivers: $215M Russia gain, $338M swing in restructuring/impairment/other (to net credit), lower tax; offset by lower gross profit and higher net interest expense (+$124M).
  - Diluted EPS $0.705 (+33%), aided by ~3% lower diluted share count from buybacks.
  - Interest income $31M (+29%); interest expense $290M (+82%) on higher USD/EUR variable rates.
  - Income tax expense $193M; effective tax rate 15.4% vs. 26.9% (lower uncertain tax provisions and non-taxable capital gain on Russia sale).
- Segment performance:
  - Flexibles: Net sales $11,154M (flat). After $516M raw material pass-through, $(404)M FX, $(207)M disposals, underlying +$98M (+1%): price/mix +4%, volumes −3%. Adjusted EBIT $1,429M (−6%); excluding FX and disposals, +$16M (+1%): price/mix +17% offset by volumes −7%, plant costs −5%, SG&A/other −4% under inflationary pressure.
  - Rigid Packaging: Net sales $3,540M (+4%); after $260M raw material pass-through and $(22)M FX, underlying −$91M (−3%): price/mix +~1%, volumes −4%. Adjusted EBIT $265M (−8%); excluding FX, −$22M (−8%): price/mix +20% more than offset by volumes −12%, plant costs −11%, SG&A/other −5%.
- Non-GAAP measures: Use of Adjusted EBIT, adjusted net income, and net debt to normalize for currency, acquisitions, restructuring, divestitures, impairments, litigation, pension settlements, hyperinflation, and Russia-Ukraine impacts; reconciliations provided.
  - Adjusted EBIT: $1,608M (FY2023) vs. $1,701M (FY2022).
  - Adjusted net income: $1,089M (FY2023) vs. $1,224M (FY2022).
- Capital structure, liquidity, and cash flows:
  - Net cash from operating activities: $1,261M (down $265M) on lower payables (inventory reduction), higher interest, and lower volumes.
  - Net cash used in investing: $(309)M (improved $218M) mainly from Russia sale proceeds offset by acquisitions/investments.
  - Net cash used in financing: $(1,025)M (higher by $134M) due to lower net debt drawdowns, partly offset by lower buybacks.
  - Net debt $6.06B (vs. $5.72B).
  - Debt facilities: $3.8B revolvers maturing 2025/2027 with two 12-month extension options; $1.3B undrawn at June 30, 2023; leverage covenant ≤3.9x; negative pledge limit 10% of tangible assets; in compliance.
  - Commercial paper outstanding $2.5B, backstopped by committed facilities.
  - Interest rate risk management: $1.25B SOFR swaps (Nov 2022–Jun 2023) at 4.53% pay-fixed; additional $1.2B swaps effective Jul 1, 2023–Jun 30, 2024 at 3.88% pay-fixed.
  - Refinancing: Issued $500M notes due 2033 at 5.63% (May 2023); redeemed €300M notes at 2.75% (Mar 2023).
  - Dividends: $723M (FY2023), continuing annual increases per share.
  - Share repurchases: $400M program completed; additional $100M authorized Feb 2023; $431M (41M shares) repurchased in FY2023; treasury share purchases for compensation $221M.
  - Credit ratings: Investment grade maintained.
- Material cash requirements:
  - Debt and interest per Note 14; leases per Note 15; pensions per Note 13.
  - Committed capex: $249M for FY2024.
  - Other purchase obligations: ~$1.1B (FY2024), then $450M, $250M, $100M, $100M (FY2025–FY2028).
  - No significant off-balance sheet obligations beyond disclosed purchases.
  - Liquidity risk management framework: minimum $200M undrawn liquidity, cash flow monitoring, diversified funding, investment policies, and staggered maturities.
- Supplemental guarantor information:
  - List of Amcor issuers/guarantors for various USD and EUR senior notes; guarantees are full, unconditional, joint and several, unsecured and unsubordinated; summary Obligor Group financials provided (FY2023 net income $1,583M including significant intercompany income; assets/liabilities detail).
- Critical accounting estimates and judgments:
  - Pensions: Assumptions for discount rate and expected return; FY2024 expense sensitivity (+/−25 bps); majority of defined benefit plans closed.
  - Goodwill and intangible assets: Annual impairment testing; key valuation assumptions; triggers for more frequent testing.
  - Deferred taxes and uncertain tax positions: Recognition thresholds, valuation allowances, and impacts of law/rate changes.
  - Valuation of assets/liabilities held for sale: Fair value estimation methods and risks, especially in conflict regions.
- New accounting pronouncements: Referenced in the notes for upcoming guidance and impacts.

structure.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.heading: Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.start_phrase: Our activities expose us to a variety of market risks and financial risks.
structure.summary:
- Scope: Item 7A summarizes Amcor’s quantitative and qualitative market risk exposures and its centralized risk management approach.
- Hedging and governance: Uses foreign exchange contracts, commodity fixed-price swaps (often on behalf of customers), interest rate swaps, cross-currency interest rate swaps, and interest rate locks to mitigate risks; activities are centrally controlled with counterparty limits and reporting; not used for speculation. Some instruments and certain foreign-currency loans used to economically hedge net investments do not qualify for U.S. GAAP hedge accounting, which can increase income statement volatility.
- Macro context: No material changes in risk profiles other than increased volatility tied to the Russia-Ukraine conflict and COVID-19.
- Interest rate risk: Manages a mix of fixed and variable debt and hedges floating exposure. Sensitivity: a 1% increase in relevant USD and EUR floating rates outstanding at June 30, 2023 would reduce FY2023 income before taxes and equity in affiliates by $20 million.
- Foreign exchange risk: Operates in 40+ countries; exposure from transactional and translational FX. Sensitivity: a 1% adverse change in the average EUR exchange rate would cut FY2023 net sales by $26 million. Sales mix by functional currency: 2023—USD 52%, EUR 18%, other currencies 30% (2022: USD 49%, EUR 17%, other 34%); translation effects vary period to period.
- Raw material and commodity price risk: Key inputs are resins, film, chemicals, aluminum, and energy. Contracts often allow pass-through of input cost changes within set periods. Sensitivity: a 1% increase in average input prices not passed to customers would raise cost of sales and reduce FY2023 income before taxes and equity in affiliates by $67 million.
- Credit risk: Arises from bank deposits, financial instruments, FX and commodity derivatives. Managed via counterparty risk policy with approved high-quality institutions and limits; no significant concentration of credit risk related to derivatives as of June 30, 2023 and 2022.

structure.start_phrase: We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Amcor plc and its subsidiaries (the “Company”) as of June 30, 2023 and 2022, and the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, equity and cash flows for each of the three years in the period ended June 30, 2023, including the related notes and schedule of valuation and qualifying accounts and reserves for each of the three years in the period ended June 30, 2023 appearing under Item 15(a)(2) (collectively referred to as the “consolidated financial statements”).
structure.summary:
- Independent auditor’s report by PricewaterhouseCoopers AG on Amcor plc’s consolidated financial statements (years ended June 30, 2021–2023) and internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) as of June 30, 2023.
- Unqualified opinions: financial statements present fairly in conformity with U.S. GAAP; ICFR effective based on COSO 2013.
- Audit conducted under PCAOB standards; auditor independence affirmed; description of audit scope, including risk assessment, testing of amounts and disclosures, evaluation of estimates and presentation, and ICFR design and operating effectiveness.
- Definition and inherent limitations of ICFR noted (reasonable assurance; potential for control deficiencies over time).
- Critical Audit Matter: goodwill impairment assessment for the Flexibles Latin America reporting unit within the Flexibles segment.
  - Context: consolidated goodwill $5,366 million; Flexibles segment goodwill $4,391 million.
  - Management uses discounted cash flow models; key assumptions include revenue growth, projected operating income growth, terminal values, and discount rate (with reference to market data and multiples).
  - CAM designation due to significant management judgment, auditor subjectivity and effort, and use of valuation specialists.
  - Auditor procedures: tested controls over the impairment process; evaluated DCF models; tested data completeness/accuracy; assessed reasonableness of key assumptions against historical performance, external market/industry data, and other audit evidence; involved specialists for valuation and discount rate assessments.
- Auditor details: PwC AG, Zurich, Switzerland; report dated August 17, 2023; auditor since 2019.
- Consolidated Statements of Income highlights (in $ millions, except per share):
  - Net sales: 2023 $14,694; 2022 $14,544; 2021 $12,861.
  - Gross profit: 2023 $2,725; 2022 $2,820; 2021 $2,732.
  - Operating income: 2023 $1,508; 2022 $1,239; 2021 $1,321.
  - Restructuring, impairment, and other related activities, net: 2023 $104; 2022 $(234); 2021 $(94).
  - Interest expense: 2023 $(290); 2022 $(159); 2021 $(153).
  - Income tax expense: 2023 $(193); 2022 $(300); 2021 $(261).
  - Net income: 2023 $1,058; 2022 $815; 2021 $951.
  - Net income attributable to Amcor plc: 2023 $1,048; 2022 $805; 2021 $939.
  - EPS: basic 2023 $0.709; 2022 $0.532; 2021 $0.604. Diluted 2023 $0.705; 2022 $0.529; 2021 $0.602.
- Reference to accompanying notes and the schedule of valuation and qualifying accounts and reserves included elsewhere in the filing.

structure.title: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements
structure.heading: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements
structure.start_phrase: Amcor plc ("Amcor" or the "Company") is a public limited company incorporated under the Laws of the Bailiwick of Jersey.
structure.summary:
- Company overview: Amcor plc is a Jersey-incorporated global packaging leader operating in two reportable segments—Flexibles and Rigid Packaging—serving food, beverage, healthcare, home and personal care, and other consumer end markets across Europe, North America, Latin America, and Asia Pacific.

- Basis of accounting: Consolidated financial statements prepared under U.S. GAAP; elimination of intercompany balances; reclassification of prior-year inventory presentation; extensive use of estimates; foreign currency translation policies; highly inflationary accounting applied to Argentina; and key revenue recognition policies including one performance obligation to supply packaging, variable consideration estimates, and practical expedients for commissions and shipping.

- Significant policies and estimates: Business combinations using acquisition method; held-for-sale and discontinued operations criteria and measurement; research and development expensed as incurred; restructuring accounting; CECL for receivables; inventory at lower of cost and NRV (FIFO/average); PP&E depreciation lives and impairment testing; lease accounting (ROU assets and liabilities); goodwill annual impairment testing (no impairment in FY2023); finite-lived intangibles amortized 1–20 years; fair value hierarchy; derivative accounting; employee benefits (defined contribution and defined benefit plans); equity method/other investments; contingencies; share-based compensation; and income tax accounting.

- New accounting guidance: Adoption of ASU 2021-10 (government assistance) with immaterial impact; disclosure adoption for supplier finance programs (ASU 2022-04).

- Restructuring, impairment, and related items:
  - FY2023 recognized a net gain of $215 million on disposal of Russian business; prior FY2022 Russia-Ukraine related impairments totaled $138 million.
  - 2023 Restructuring Plan: expected total cost $200–$220 million; projects of ~$150 million initiated in FY2023 with $65m employee, $13m fixed asset, $10m other, $6m related costs; largely to be completed by end of FY2024.
  - 2019 Bemis Integration Plan completed in FY2022 (total $253m).
  - 2018 Rigid Packaging Plan completed in FY2021 ($121m).
  - Aggregate restructuring and related expenses over plans total $547 million to date.

- Acquisitions and divestitures (FY2023):
  - Acquisitions: Czech flexible packaging plant ($59m; $23m goodwill); Shanghai medical device packaging site ($60m incl. $20m contingent; $39m goodwill; preliminary); New Zealand automated protein packaging machine maker ($45m incl. $13m contingent; $36m goodwill; preliminary). Pro forma impact immaterial.
  - Disposal: Russian business sold for $365m net cash, generating $215m pre-tax gain; prior impairment of $90m recorded in FY2022. Russian assets were previously classified as held for sale.

- Held for sale: Russian operations classified as held for sale in Q4 FY2022 and sold in December 2022; did not qualify as discontinued operations.

- Equity method and other investments: $89m total as of June 30, 2023; largest is ePac Holdings, LLC (18.9% ownership; $33m; equity method with three-month reporting lag); AMVIG interest sold in FY2021 (gain recorded previously).

- PP&E and intangible assets:
  - PP&E, net: $3,762m; depreciation expense ~$395m in FY2023.
  - Goodwill: $5,366m (Flexibles $4,391m; Rigid $975m); changes reflect acquisitions, FX, and Russian disposal allocation.
  - Other intangibles, net: $1,524m; FY2023 amortization $174m; estimated future amortization ~$173m in FY2024 trending modestly lower thereafter.

- Fair value measurements: Disclosure of Level 1–3 hierarchy; long-term fixed-rate debt fair value below carrying value; derivatives and contingent consideration measured at fair value with Level 3 contingent consideration liabilities of $46m (primarily FY2023 acquisitions).

- Derivatives and risk management: Use of interest rate swaps (economic hedges of commercial paper), FX forwards (cash flow hedges and non-designated), and commodity hedges (aluminum; previously PET). Effects on AOCI and income presented; notional balances reduced in FX forwards year over year.

- Pension and employee benefits:
  - Mix of funded/unfunded defined benefit plans primarily in U.S., Switzerland, UK, Germany; many closed to new entrants.
  - U.S. defined benefit plan termination announced (July 31, 2023) with expected distributions starting FY2025; likely settlement accounting then.
  - FY2023 funded status deficit $(163)m; contributions expected $29m next year; benefit payments elevated in FY2025 due to U.S. plan termination.
  - Asset allocation across equities, debt, real estate, insurance contracts; detail of Level 3 movements.

- Debt and liquidity:
  - Total debt $6,666m (including commercial paper classified long-term due to backstop facilities); issued $500m 2033 notes at 5.63% in May 2023; redeemed €300m bonds at maturity in March 2023 funded with commercial paper.
  - Syndicated revolving credit facilities total $3.8b (tranches maturing 2025 and 2027 with extension options); ~$1.3b undrawn at year-end; leverage covenant ≤3.9x—compliant.
  - Short-term debt mainly bank loans/overdrafts ($80m).

- Leases: Operating lease ROU assets $533m; total lease liabilities $614m; FY2023 total lease expense $154m; weighted-average remaining term ~8 years for operating leases.

- Shareholders’ equity:
  - Ongoing share repurchases/cancellations; treasury share activity to satisfy equity awards.
  - AOCI components and reclassifications disclosed (FX translation, pension, derivatives); notable recycling of $73m FX translation losses on Russian disposal.
  - Forward contracts to purchase own shares outstanding at June 30, 2023 for 9m shares at avg $12.39 to hedge delivery under employee plans.

- Income taxes:
  - FY2023 effective tax rate 15.4% (benefited from non-taxable Russian disposal gain and release of uncertain tax positions); FY2022: 26.9%.
  - Deferred tax net liability $(482)m; valuation allowances maintained where realization not more likely than not; ~$1.3b NOLs and $37m credits (mostly non-expiring).
  - Unrecognized tax benefits $155m; audits ongoing in multiple jurisdictions.

- Share-based compensation: Mix of options, RSUs, performance rights/shares, and share rights; FY2023 expense $54m; unrecognized cost $71m (1.8-year average amortization); option activity summarized.

- Earnings per share: Two-class method; FY2023 basic EPS $0.709; diluted $0.705; diluted shares impacted by repurchases and forward contracts; anti-dilutive awards disclosed.

- Contingencies:
  - Brazil tax matters with $14m accrual and $26m additional reasonably possible loss; collateral posted under local rules.
  - Environmental accruals $63m in total; no individual environmental proceeding above $1m threshold requiring SEC disclosure.
  - Ordinary-course legal matters not expected to be material.

- Segments and performance:
  - FY2023 net sales $14,694m (Flexibles $11,154m; Rigid $3,540m).
  - Adjusted EBIT $1,608m (Flexibles $1,429m; Rigid $265m; Other $(86)m); reconciliation to GAAP income includes restructuring, amortization, hyperinflation, Russia-Ukraine impacts, pension settlements, and other items.
  - Capex $526m; depreciation and amortization $569m; geographic sales breakdown provided.

- Deed of Cross Guarantee (Australia): Lists participating subsidiaries; provides ASIC-required condensed financial statements for the closed group.

- Supplemental cash flow information: Interest paid $276m; income taxes paid $225m; non-cash capex accruals and contingent/deferred acquisition liabilities disclosed.

- Subsequent events:
  - July 2023 UK pension buy-in policy (~$60m of plan assets/obligations).
  - August 10, 2023 agreement to acquire a small flexible packaging manufacturer in India.
  - August 16, 2023 dividend declaration of $0.1225 per share (with ASX settlement waiver timing note).
